hook: Dream sweep Liberty, reach first Finals in *13* years
dek: Atlanta completes a 3-0 sweep of New York, heading to its first Finals since 2013.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: The Atlanta Dream beat the New York Liberty *85-83*, completing a 3-0 sweep of the WNBA semifinals.

slides.label: Big picture
slides.text: It's Atlanta's first Finals trip in *13 years*, since 2013, under first-year head coach Karl Smesko.

slides.label: Reese's night
slides.text: Angel Reese scored *22 points* with 9 rebounds and 2 blocks, battling Jonquel Jones, who had 26 points.

slides.label: Howard & Canada
slides.text: Rhyne Howard added *21 points* while Jordin Canada ran the offense with 19 points and 11 assists.

slides.label: Liberty's comeback
slides.text: New York trailed by 12 in the third quarter, then used a *17-4 run* to take the lead late.

slides.label: Final seconds
slides.text: Breanna Stewart missed a layup with 9 seconds left, then DeWanna Bonner hit two free throws to seal it.

slides.label: Short-handed
slides.text: Allisha Gray missed her second straight game with a *left finger injury*, yet Atlanta still won.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: A team built on depth, not one star, shows underrepresented athletes can win on teamwork over hype.

question: Can the Dream win it all? Yes or no.
first_comment: Bonner's two free throws with 6.2 seconds left sealed the win. Who shows up big in the Finals?
photo_caption: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream after sweeping the New York Liberty 3-0.
caption_instagram:
The Atlanta Dream are headed to the WNBA Finals for the first time in 13 years after sweeping the New York Liberty 3-0, closing it out 85-83 on Friday night, according to Rolling Out.

Angel Reese led the way with 22 points, 9 rebounds and 2 blocks, going toe to toe with Jonquel Jones all night. Rhyne Howard scored 21, and Jordin Canada ran the show with 19 points and 11 assists after New York clawed back from a 12-point deficit. Atlanta held on in the final seconds, with DeWanna Bonner sinking two free throws to secure the win, and they did it all without Allisha Gray, sidelined by a finger injury.

The Dream open the Finals on Oct. 17 against the winner of Aces vs. Valkyries, chasing their first title in franchise history.

Can the Dream win it all? Yes or no.
